title: Reduction of the proper bound to a lattice on a stratum
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Qlb$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ of $\Qlb$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,Y$ be separated schemes of finite type over $k$, as in [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting], let $p\colon X\to Y$ be a proper $k$-morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $c\in\mathbf Z$. Put $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$. For finite subextensions $F/\mathbf Q_\ell$ of $\Qlb$ and their rings of integers use their condensed topological rings [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]; for $\Qlb$ use the finite-subextension-valued condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed]. For each coefficient ring $A$ below, $A_T$ denotes its pulled-back condensed ring on the small pro-étale site [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients], and modules are module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects]. Write $R^qp_*$ for the right derived functors of the additive left exact module pushforward [def-sfb-module-lower-star], with $R^qp_*=0$ for $q<0$.

For a locally closed immersion $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion], write $a_!=i_*u_!$, where $u\colon S\hookrightarrow\overline S$ is open and $i\colon\overline S\hookrightarrow X$ is closed, as in [sk-lem-coefficient-heart]. Lisse finite free means locally free of finite rank for the pro-étale topology, with ranks allowed to vary. For an $\mathcal O_{F,T}$-module $N$, set $N[1/\ell]=F_T\otimes_{\mathcal O_{F,T}}N$, and for an $F_T$-module $P$ put $P_{\Qlb}=\Qlb_T\otimes_{F_T}P$; these are ordinary extension-of-scalars functors [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] along the coefficient maps [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change].

Suppose that for every locally closed immersion $a\colon S\hookrightarrow X$, every finite extension $F/E$ inside $\Qlb$ (including $F=E$), and every lisse finite free $\mathcal O_{F,S}$-module $L_0$, one has
$$R^qp_*(a_!L_0)=0\qquad(q>c),$$
and that this vanishing also holds for $(a_!L_0)[1/\ell]$ and for $((a_!L_0)[1/\ell])_{\Qlb}$. Then
$$R^qp_*M=0\qquad(q>c)$$
for every $M\in\Cons(X,\Lambda)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible].

proof.text: For each coefficient ring used here, apply [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist] to the small pro-étale site, in a universe in which it is small, and its actual pulled-back coefficient sheaf. Its module category is Grothendieck abelian; [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] supplies enough injectives. The functor $p_*$ is additive and left exact by [def-sfb-module-lower-star]. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact] applies to any short exact sequence $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$. For $q\ge0$ it gives the exact segment $R^qp_*M'\to R^qp_*M\to R^qp_*M''$. If $q>c$ and both outer terms vanish, the middle term is zero. For negative $q$ all three functors are zero by convention. Starting with the zero sheaf, induction on the length of a finite filtration therefore propagates the bound from its quotients to the sheaf.

The scheme $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]: $\operatorname{Spec}k$ is Noetherian since a field has only the ideals $0,k$. A locally closed subscheme $S$ is closed in an open $V\subset X$ by [def-weil-closed-immersion]. The open $V$ is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]. Choose finitely many distinguished affine opens of finite-type affine charts of $X$ covering $V$; their rings are finitely generated $k$-algebras (a localization at $f$ adjoins one generator $f^{-1}$). The corresponding charts of $S$ have quotient rings, again finitely generated. Thus $S$ is finite type over $k$. It is separated: its diagonal is the inverse image of the closed diagonal of $X$ under $S\times_kS\to X\times_kX$. On charts this equality follows by imposing equality of the two coordinate maps and then their quotient relations; an immersion has no two different lifts of the same point or scheme map. The closed-diagonal criterion is [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Hence $S$ is a standing scheme, and is Noetherian by the same finite-type theorem. The same argument applies to a closed subscheme such as the closure of $S$. All these schemes are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated].

source.place: Strata and Lattices: verify the ambient hypotheses on every stratum.

proof.text:
For every finite coefficient field $F$ and scheme $T$, [sk-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x] identifies $F_T$ with $\mathcal O_{F,T}[1/\ell]$. By the balanced tensor universal property [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars],
$$F_T\otimes_{\mathcal O_{F,T}}N\cong\varinjlim(N\xrightarrow{\ell}N\xrightarrow{\ell}\cdots).$$
Indeed a map out of the tensor is a compatible family of $\mathcal O_{F,T}$-linear maps from $N$, with the $r$th copy representing $\ell^{-r}\otimes N$; this also gives its inverse. Filtered colimits are exact by [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist], so this localization is exact. Finite field scalar change is exact by [lem-sfb-subfield-flat], and extension to $\Qlb$ is exact by [lem-sfb-qlbar-flat]: those statements supply finite-limit preservation, while the extension-of-scalars left adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars] supplies finite colimits. By [def-sfb-left-derived-exact], all these left derived functors agree with their ordinary termwise functors. We may therefore use [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] on degree-zero modules once the relevant extension by zero has also been checked exact.

source.place: Lattices: exact ordinary scalar change and its agreement with derived scalar change.

proof.text: Choose a finite stratification adapted to $M$ using the constructible/lisse characterization in [sk-lem-coefficient-heart], and write $L=M|_S$ on an initial stratum. Step 2 verifies that $S$ is a standing scheme. For $\Lambda=E$, put $F=E$ and $L_F=L$. For $\Lambda=\Qlb$, [sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit] (1) gives a finite subextension $F_0/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and a lisse $L_{F_0}$ with $(L_{F_0})_{\Qlb}\cong L$. Replace $F_0$ by the compositum $F=EF_0$ inside $\Qlb$. This is finite: products of finite bases span a finite-dimensional subalgebra containing both fields; multiplication by any nonzero element is injective, hence surjective, so this algebra is itself a field. Put $L_F=F_S\otimes_{F_{0,S}}L_{F_0}$. Local free trivializations remain local free trivializations of the same rank after scalar change. Transitivity [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (3), interpreted ordinarily by Step 3, identifies $(L_F)_{\Qlb}$ with $L$. Thus every field to which we will apply the premise is a finite extension of the fixed $E$.

source.place: Strata: descend the lisse restrictions and enlarge their coefficient field to contain E.

proof.text: Apply [sk-lem-stratified-lattice] on each initial stratum to the lisse $L_F$ of Step 4. It gives finitely many locally closed pieces with lisse $\mathcal O_F$-lattices $L_0$ and $L_0[1/\ell]\cong L_F$ there. Their union is a finite locally closed stratification of $X$. This assertion respects scheme structures: write $S$ closed in $V\subset X$ open, and a lattice piece closed in $U\subset S$ open; choose $W\subset V$ open with $U=S\cap W$. Then $U$ is closed in $W$, and the lattice piece is closed in $W$ because the two quotient maps of rings compose to a quotient map. This uses the immersion description in [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Apply [det-lem-coefficient-heart-common-stratification] (1) to order a refinement as $T_1,\ldots,T_m$ with $V_j=\bigcup_{i\le j}T_i$ open in $X$. Restrict each chosen lattice to its refined piece. Pullback coefficients and restriction are the exact inverse-image lift by [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] (1), so a restricted local free basis stays a basis. Restriction of $L_0[1/\ell]\cong L_F$ remains that equality, by [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (1) and Step 3. The same clause identifies restriction of $(L_F)_{\Qlb}$ with scalar extension of its restriction. Hence $M|_{T_i}$ is the localized lattice in the $E$ case, and its $\Qlb$ scalar extension in the other case.

source.place: Lattices: refine lattice strata globally and restrict their models.

proof.text: For each final stratum $b_i:T_i\hookrightarrow X$, write $b_i=i\circ u$, with $u:T_i\hookrightarrow\overline{T_i}$ open and $i:\overline{T_i}\hookrightarrow X$ closed. Step 2 makes $X$ and $\overline{T_i}$ qcqs. Every open in these Noetherian schemes is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]; thus $u$ and the open complement of $i$ are quasi-compact. Apply [det-sf-open-closed-sequence-ring-sheaf] to $u$ and its closed complement on $\overline{T_i}$, and to $i$ and its open complement on $X$. Its clauses (1) and (2) make $u_!$ and $i_*$ exact. By [sk-prop-sfb-cartesian-coefficients] (1), the restricted rings are precisely the prescribed pulled-back coefficient rings. This applies to $\mathcal O_F,F,\Qlb$, so $b_{i!}=i_*u_!$ is exact in every required coefficient category. Consequently clause (2) of [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] gives sheaf-level scalar comparisons, by Step 3. Its commutative-ring hypothesis holds for all these rings, and its standing-scheme hypothesis holds for $X,T_i$ by Step 2.

source.place: Lattices: exact locally closed extension and the hypotheses of scalar compatibility.

proof.text: Apply [det-lem-coefficient-heart-filtration] directly to $M$ and the ordered adapted stratification of Step 5. Since $X$ is Noetherian and $\Lambda=E$ or $\Qlb$, it gives a finite filtration with quotients $b_{i!}(M|_{T_i})$. Choose the lattice $L_{0,i}$ over its field $F$ from Step 5. In the $E$ case $F=E$, and [det-prop-scalar-six-pullback] (2) identifies the quotient with $(b_{i!}L_{0,i})[1/\ell]$. In the $\Qlb$ case use that clause first along $\mathcal O_F\to F$ and then along $F\to\Qlb$ to identify it with $((b_{i!}L_{0,i})[1/\ell])_{\Qlb}$. Steps 3 and 6 justify these comparisons on sheaves. The premise applies to each immersion, finite field extension $F/E$, and lisse finite free lattice, so every quotient satisfies the bound. The finite-filtration induction of Step 1 now proves $R^qp_*M=0$ for all $q>c$.

source.place: Lattices and Extensions: identify the actual filtration quotients and conclude.

split_report.summary: Retained the previous statement and lattice route; checked every cited current statement. Separated the long scalar, geometric, and filtration arguments into seven steps and reused existing subfield and algebraic-closure flatness lemmas instead of hiding those comparisons inline. Generated current verbatim witnesses for every citation. No new nodes and no statement change.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes Extensions; Steps 2 and 4 realize Strata and its ambient hypotheses; Steps 3 and 5–7 realize Lattices, including exact scalar change, global refinement, extension-by-zero comparison, and the final filtration induction.

tool_uses.why: The general ringed-site theorem supplies Grothendieck module categories on the actual pro-étale coefficient sheaves; this ambient homological input is not a step of the proper-bound unit.
Enough injectives for a Grothendieck category verifies the hypothesis of the long-exact-sequence tool.
The general derived-functor long exact sequence supplies extension stability; no node of this proper-bound unit states this homological fact.
Generic finite-type Noetherianity verifies the hypotheses of the existing stratification and filtration tools.
Generic Noetherian-open quasi-compactness verifies that locally closed strata remain finite type over k.
Generic ordering and refinement of finite strata implements the refinement already required in the proper-bound route.
Generic filtration with specified stratum quotients implements the open–closed dévissage required by the unit.

Generic coefficient-change compatibility with restriction and extension by zero identifies the lattice and target-coefficient pieces; the proper-bound unit has no separate statement of this compatibility.
The generic pulled-back coefficient colimits give localization and the filtered finite-field union used to identify ordinary and derived scalar change.
Cartesian coefficients identify the restricted rings in the localization tool, and finite freeness proves exactness of finite field scalar change.
Generic quasi-separatedness checks the qcqs hypotheses of the arbitrary-ring localization tool.
The generic ring-sheaf theorem proves exactness of open extension and closed direct image also for integral coefficients; the rational coefficient-heart statement alone does not supply that case.
Finite-field scalar extension exactness is a generic coefficient tool needed for the scalar comparison, without replacing the lattice route.
Algebraic-closure scalar extension exactness is the existing generic flatness input explicitly required by the blueprint Lattices paragraph.

The delivery re-splits the already reviewed item into 7 steps: statement and stmt_deps are unchanged, there are no new nodes, and the unit record is untouched. Statement: compared with the main-20261015 .md, it covers every F/E in Qlb including F=E, its 'also holds' is equivalent to the source's 'passes to', and it adds the standing setting explicitly. It is not weakened. It is a lemma, not a target, so there is no base-change morphism to check; the coefficients are module objects over the pulled-back O_F, F and Qlb throughout. Checks by step: S1, the Grothendieck module category from prop-pur-kinjective plus enough injectives make the long exact sequence of lem-weil-pbc-derived-functor-long-exact apply, and R^q=0 for q<0 covers negative c. S2, X is Noetherian, strata are finite type (localization and quotient charts) and separated (S->X is a monomorphism, so the diagonal is a base change of the closed one), and qcqs. S3, F_T=O_F[1/l] from qlbar-colimit-x, tensor = l-colimit (checked through the universal property), lem-sfb-subfield-flat and lem-sfb-qlbar-flat plus the left adjoint give exactness, and LF=D(F) holds because sk-def-sfb-coefficient-change defines the tensor as L(Ext). S4, only clause (1) of the two-colimit theorem is used, and the compositum EF_0 is a field. S5, the stratified lattice is lisse = locally free of finite rank, as the premise needs; the immersion composition is written out, and the ordered refinement comes from common-stratification (1). S6, u_! and i_* are exact for an arbitrary ring sheaf on qcqs schemes, and coherence gives a_!=i_*u_!. S7, the filtration quotients a_k!(M|S_k), transported by scalar-six (2) once or twice, are exactly the sheaves the premise covers. Small cases: X empty, rank 0, a point with c=0 and c=-1, different fields on different strata. Graph: proof_deps equals the union of step uses, every id exists and none is merged, and a DFS finds no cycle. rg over the DAG finds no duplicate; the only related node, det-proper-heart-bound-rational, consumes this item. No SGA. I accept the two new tool_uses, lem-sfb-subfield-flat and lem-sfb-qlbar-flat: the blueprint's Lattices paragraph invokes this flatness itself and sk-thm-sfb-qlbar-two-colimit cites the same two nodes.

reviewed_lean.note: Clause-by-clause match of properHeartBoundReduction with the node and blueprint source: prime ell; k with CharP r prime, r≠ell; X,Y separated finite type over k; p IsProper over k; c:ℤ. R^q tested for q:ℕ with c<q, so negative degrees vanish by convention and degree 0 is tested for c<0. Conclusion covers Λ=E or finite-subextension-valued Q̄ℓ and all ConstantModelConstructible M.
